subject: Scheduler canary: explicit rollback criteria + on-call staffing (runtime-1.19)
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Scheduler canary: explicit rollback criteria + on-call staffing (runtime-1.19)

Team,

Before SRE signs off on the mixed-workload scheduler canary (runtime-1.19, flag on), we need two items made explicit and captured in ENG-4829 / runbook:

1) Rollback criteria (quantitative) with a clear owner + decision path
2) On-call staffing plan (who is primary, who is shadow, and who has rollback permissions)

Right now the canary plan reads as "monitor p95 and queue depth" but not specific enough to page/rollback without a debate.

Please reply with:
- Proposed rollback triggers (p95/p99, error rate, queue depth growth, starvation indicators)
- Exact dashboards to pin (links)
- Coverage plan: hours, timezone, and backstop

Links I’m using:
- Draft dashboards: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/rt-mixed-sched/mixed-workload-scheduler-canary
- Tail guidance: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Latency+SLO+Tail+Breakdown+Guidance
- ENG-4829: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4829/canary-plan-rollback-criteria

Attaching the approval checklist we’ll use for the go/no-go.

Attachment: Scheduler_Canary_Approval_Checklist_v3.pdf

—
Neha Kapoor
SRE Director, Redwood Inference



From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Peter Holtz <peter.holtz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Scheduler canary: explicit rollback criteria + on-call staffing (runtime-1.19)

Neha—ack. We can tighten this today.

Proposed rollback triggers for first canary slice (Dedicated us-west-2, 5% traffic on 2 routes):

Hard rollback (flip flag OFF immediately):
- p95 end-to-end latency for "short/interactive" class regresses > 15% vs baseline for 10+ minutes (A/B in same window)
- request timeout rate increases > 0.25% absolute over baseline for 5+ minutes
- starvation guardrail: long-queue max_wait > 45s for 3 consecutive 1m buckets (this is new metric)

Soft rollback (pause and investigate, but default is to rollback unless root cause is external):
- sustained queue_depth_short > 3x baseline for 10+ minutes
- GPU utilization dips > 8% while queue_depth increases (suggests scheduler lock contention / batching pathology)

Dashboards:
- Mixed scheduler canary: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/rt-mixed-sched/mixed-workload-scheduler-canary
- Latency tail breakdown: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/sre-latency-tail/latency-tail-breakdown

We’ll add these thresholds to the runbook and ENG-4829.

Coverage: Rafael primary during canary window; I can be shadow + have immediate rollback permissions. We’ll ask Sean if he wants a formal SRE backstop.

—
Sofia
Engineering Manager, Runtime Scheduling



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Peter Holtz <peter.holtz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:29 AM PT
Subject: Re: Scheduler canary: explicit rollback criteria + on-call staffing (runtime-1.19)

+1 to making it crisp.

Two tweaks:
- The p95 regression should be measured on the same cohort (flag ON) vs control (flag OFF) AND normalized for request size. If we can’t normalize quickly, we at least split by class (short/long) so we don’t get fooled by prompt mix shifts.
- Add a hard rollback on "error budget burn" for the route SLO if it spikes (even if p95 looks better).

Neha: for staffing, I want an SRE named as incident commander (IC) for the window. Rafael is a good pick.

Also: ensure rollback is a single toggle in config, not a redeploy.

—
Sean Gallagher
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference



From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Peter Holtz <peter.holtz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:11 AM PT
Subject: Re: Scheduler canary: explicit rollback criteria + on-call staffing (runtime-1.19)

I can be IC for the canary window.

Proposed staffing:
- IC (SRE): Rafael (PT)
- SRE secondary: Aisha (ET) for overlap + alert tuning
- Runtime on-point: Sofia
- Runtime secondary (config/rollbacks): Peter (for admission control knobs)

Rollback permissions:
- Rafael + Sofia both have access to flip the runtime scheduler flag for the canary slice (via canary config)
- Connor on standby if release-train tooling is weird

I’ll update the runbook with an explicit "Rollback steps" section + links to the config page and the exact flag name.

Draft runbook location (will fill in today): https://runbooks.redwoodinference.com/runtime/scheduler-canary-rollback



From: Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:02 PM PT
Subject: Re: Scheduler canary: explicit rollback criteria + on-call staffing (runtime-1.19)

Adding alerting details so we don’t invent thresholds live.

I’ll set (temporary) canary-scoped alerts routed to #eng-sre + paging IC only for hard rollback triggers:

P0 (page):
- short_class p95 latency regression > 15% vs control for 10 minutes
- timeout_rate delta > +0.25% for 5 minutes
- long_class starvation: max_wait > 45s for 3 minutes

P1 (no page; Slack + investigate):
- queue_depth_short > 3x baseline for 10 minutes
- backlog_growth_rate positive for 10 minutes while GPU util < baseline

One question: metric naming. The new starvation metric is currently emitted as:
- runtime.scheduler.queue.long.max_wait_ms
We should confirm this matches the dashboard queries. Sofia/Peter can you confirm final names?



From: Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 8:37 AM PT
Subject: Re: Scheduler canary: explicit rollback criteria + on-call staffing (runtime-1.19)

I reviewed the checklist attachment. Two additions I recommend for operational safety:

- Explicit "stop-the-line" clause: IC can rollback without additional approvals if any P0 triggers hit.
- Add a "known confounders" section in the runbook (e.g., capacity events, model rollout, kernel change) so we don’t misattribute.

Also please include the exact canary slice definition:
- cluster(s)
- route(s)
- % traffic
- start/end time

If you want, I can draft that section in the ops plan doc.

Attachment: runtime-1.19-canary-ops-plan.docx

—
Tomáš Novák
SRE, Runbooks & Incident Readiness



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Peter Holtz <peter.holtz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 3:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Scheduler canary: explicit rollback criteria + on-call staffing (runtime-1.19)

Thanks all. This is close.

Remaining gaps to close before SRE approval:

1) Put the hard/soft rollback criteria into ENG-4829 verbatim (copy/paste from Sofia/Aisha) and link the dashboard panels that correspond to each criterion.
2) Confirm metric names (Aisha’s point). If there’s any renaming risk between now and runtime-1.19 cut, freeze names for the canary.
3) Runbook must include:
- exact flag name
- exact slice definition
- rollback steps that take < 2 minutes
- "stop-the-line" clause (Tomáš)

Rafael: please assign yourself IC in the ticket and list the staffing plan (including backstop).

Sofia: once metric names are confirmed, reply here with the final set and I’ll mark SRE sign-off.



From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Peter Holtz <peter.holtz@redwoodinference.com>

Final metric names confirmed (frozen for canary):
- runtime.scheduler.queue.short.depth
- runtime.scheduler.queue.long.depth
- runtime.scheduler.queue.short.wait_ms (histogram)
- runtime.scheduler.queue.long.wait_ms (histogram)
- runtime.scheduler.queue.long.max_wait_ms (gauge)  <-- starvation guardrail
- runtime.requests.timeout_rate
- runtime.latency.e2e_ms{class=short|long} (derived from tracing spans)

ENG-4829 updated with:
- hard/soft rollback criteria
- staffing plan (Rafael IC; Aisha secondary; Sofia on-point; Peter secondary; Connor backstop)
- links to the exact Grafana panels

Ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4829/canary-plan-rollback-criteria

Runbook updated with "stop-the-line" clause + rollback steps (flip flag + verify control cohort in 2m):
https://runbooks.redwoodinference.com/runtime/scheduler-canary-rollback

Neha: can you confirm SRE approval so we can keep the runtime-1.19 timeline?

—
Sofia
